title: Trump Declares 'Total Control' of Hormuz, Warns Iran Could 'Get Blown Away'
detail: President Trump told reporters at Joint Base Andrews that the US has 'total control' of the Strait of Hormuz, calling the naval blockade a 'wall of steel' and saying 'at some point, maybe they'll do something, and then they get blown away.' Trump said US forces had swept the waterway for mines, meaning it is now 'open,' but shipping traffic remained near collapsed levels — just 8 vessels transited on Tuesday versus 130-140/day before the war. Iran rejected the claim: new Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei said the strait will not reopen until the war and naval blockade end, sanctions are lifted, US forces withdraw from the region, Iran receives reparations, and the wars in Lebanon and Gaza end.

media.caption: Trump again says the US has 'control' of the Strait of Hormuz as transit numbers keep dropping

title: Oil Prices Rise as Deadly Attacks Dim Hopes for Hormuz Reopening
detail: Brent crude climbed after the Aug 11 US strike on the blockade-running Vela Nova and the fatal Houthi 'double-tap' attack on the Tihamah deepened doubts that a Strait of Hormuz reopening was imminent. The IEA's monthly report warned of a 1.8 million bpd global oil-market shortfall this quarter as the conflict persists.

media.caption: Oil prices rise as attacks dent hopes for Strait of Hormuz reopening

title: US and Iran Agree in Principle to Extend 60-Day Islamabad MOU Ceasefire Ahead of Aug 17 Deadline
detail: Pakistani government sources said Washington and Tehran have conveyed consent to mediators to extend the 60-day ceasefire framework under the June 17 Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, which is due to expire August 17. The two sides are still exchanging messages through Pakistani intermediaries to settle on an extension period. The underlying MOU talks have been stalled for weeks over disagreements on security guarantees and freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran's naval blockade of the strait has continued throughout.

media.caption: US and Iran agree to extend 60-day ceasefire, Pakistani sources say
